rubric_notes: Good conceptual treatment of fold vs superfamily vs family, homology inference and function-transfer limits. However it omits the bacterial histone-fold family (a.22.1.4), a must_include entity; archaeal histone placement is left vague ('with the histone-fold family or its close relatives') rather than the separate family a.22.1.2; family name given as 'Nucleosomal histones' rather than 'Nucleosome core histones'; no release (2.08) cited and no evidence bundle. Lists Dpb3/Dpb4, CENP-S/X, CENP-T/W, TAF8/TAF10, TAF11/TAF13 as superfamily members without SCOPe support. Hedges family numbering honestly, so no fabrication. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Central conclusion correct: same superfamily a.204.1, different families, probable common ancestry, no function transfer. However never gives the family sccs a.204.1.2 / a.204.1.4 (must_include item 1), mislabels superfamily and fold as 'MazG-like' rather than 'all-alpha NTP pyrophosphatases', relies on memory with no evidence, and asserts a conserved acidic metal-binding motif as SCOPe's basis without support. Suffix-'1' explanation imprecise. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Biological inference is complete: superfamily-level remote homology, conserved two-subdomain ATP-binding core, explicit limits on substrate, reaction, physiological role, oligomeric state, regulation and template use, and correct statement that fold c.55 alone would not establish homology. However the answer never gives the family identifiers c.55.1.1, c.55.1.3, c.55.1.4 (required by must_include) and wrongly suggests the family numbers vary by release. No evidence bundle. Factual support limited to superfamily/fold/class. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Biological reasoning is complete: remote homology within one superfamily, divergence on a shared di-metal scaffold, explicit refusal to transfer function/metal/mechanism/quaternary structure, template limits, and required evidence (active-site conservation, metal-ligand pattern, assembly, metal content, assays). Factual support is thin: no release or SUNIDs, only a.25.1.1 given explicitly while the a.25.1.2 and a.25.1.3 family codes required by the question are omitted, and rubrerythrin is called a separate family within the fold rather than a protein under a.25.1.1. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Good inference: superfamily records common descent not shared activity, functional divergence does not contradict the classification, copper/electron transfer not transferable, evidence requirements listed. But memory-based with no bundle, no release, and omits the required family identifiers b.6.1.5 and b.6.1.6 (only b.6.1.1 given). Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Strong reasoning: superfamily-level common ancestry on shared beta-grasp core, family boundaries mark functional divergence with correct mechanisms, explicit rejection of conjugation, UBX->Ras, RBD->p97, interface/specificity transfer, and fold-level over-extension. Factual support weak: no evidence bundle, no release, family SCCS codes and sunids not given (acknowledged as from memory).

Correctly names fold c.23 and superfamily c.23.1 and gives a sound account of why CheY phosphotransfer, ODC catalysis, KaiA clock function and CheY-derived templates cannot be transferred. However it names none of the three family sccs (c.23.1.1/c.23.1.4/c.23.1.5) and explicitly hedges on whether the ODC wing is even in the CheY-like superfamily, so the required supported relationship is only partially established. No evidence bundle. Factual error in background: assigns ODC catalysis to a TIM-barrel domain in fold c.1.6 with a C-terminal beta-barrel, which is the eukaryotic ODC architecture; the ODC whose wing is c.23.1.4 (Lactobacillus 30a) has a c.67.1.5 major domain and d.125.1.1 C-terminal domain. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Correctly says fold-level grouping is structural only and homology is claimed only among V/A-type A-subunit bulge domains. But it confuses the family-versus-superfamily distinction: it says the classification 'should not be read as a family-level claim' because the A subunit's other domains are classified separately, which misstates the hierarchy (b.84.5.1 is a family-level homology claim; other domains' placement is irrelevant). No sccs, sunid or release cited; admits pretrained knowledge only. Must_include 1 and 3 unmet. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct conclusion: shared fold f.21, three separate superfamilies, fold membership carries no ancestry claim; convergence raised as an alternative and the answer is calibrated ('similar fold, no demonstrated homology'). Names the independent evidence needed (sequence/profile, conserved heme-ligand and interface positions, gene context) and rejects function/template transfer. Factual support is thin: the three superfamilies are named but the f.21.1/f.21.2/f.21.3 identifiers required by must_include are never given, no sunids, no release, no evidence bundle. All stated facts are correct. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Biological reasoning complete: superfamily c.2.1 = probable distant common ancestor, separate families = remote relationship and divergent function, explicit rejection of transferring substrate, cofactor specificity, catalytic activity or physiological role; notes separate GroES-like catalytic domain and partner domains; lists family-level evidence needed. No evidence bundle; gives c.2 and c.2.1 from memory but omits all three family sccs required by must_include. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

No lookup performed; answer is generic reasoning about designed proteins with hedged 'if SCOPe places them under the same catch-all node'. Does not state the shared family k.40.1.1, sunid 100905, or the 'not a true family' annotation. Reaches a defensible but unsupported conclusion and drifts toward asserting convergence. Honest about not having verified. Evidence sparse: factual 1; mostly generic principle without the requested specific inference: bio 1.

Direction of change (separate fold/superfamily in 1.69 to shared c.23.14 superfamily, separate families now) and probable-common-ancestry interpretation with function/template caveats are correct. No evidence retrieved; no SIDs, no 1.69 sccs (c.137.1.1), family sccs explicitly unknown. Hedged appropriately but factual support is sparse and unverified. No must_avoid violations.

Recall-only, hedged. Places d1a14h2 in class l Artifacts and correctly identifies d1a14h1 as VH in Ig superfamily/fold, class b, but never gives SCCS l.1.1.1, the Tags lineage, or 'Synthetic', saying only 'expect sccs to start with l.'. Central conclusion (tag similarity is not homology, infer from d1a14h1) is correct with limits, but 'antibody-framework N-terminal sequence' muddles artifact vs native residues. Evidence sparse.
Pretrained-only, empty bundle, no specific sids, boundaries, or release change. Correct general module and per-domain homology-search reasoning, but it does not answer the specific 1acc change.

Answered from memory with no SIDs, boundaries or sccs. Wrong domain composition: lists a Jab1/MPN domain among the five (not part of 3jb9 chain A's five SCOPe domains) and omits the bromodomain d3jb9a4. d.394 never named. Mosaic concept, N-terminal new fold, and no-function-transfer caveats are correct, but the wrong domain set caps biological reasoning at 2. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 judge, 2026-10-22.

Repeat-count logic is right, but no evidence retrieved; misidentifies 2kq5 as a dHax3 NMR structure (it is PthA), misnames fold a.298 as 'TAL effector-like', speculates about Ralstonia. No 're' flag or representative repeat unit, so must_include item 3 is unmet.

No endpoint access; reports no endpoint values at all (2.08 given only as an example, no periodic label), so the first must_include is unmet. Semantics are correct and well stated: stable release frozen and primary citation, cite exact dated periodic label when periodic-only entries are used, do not cite 'latest'/'current', periodic adds newly released PDB structures and is not a new stable version. No fabrication; honest about limits. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 judge, 2026-10-22.

Evaluator Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. No evidence retrieved; works from recall and hedges 'same family or superfamily' without naming a.47.2.1 or any SIDs/sunids. Misnames fold a.47 as 'spectrin-repeat-like' (it is STAT-like). General fragment-bias reasoning (fragments should not define fold, prefer complete domain, revisit) is sound and avoids the must_avoid errors, but the SCOPe fragment comment and 'ms' flag are absent, so the specific fragment-driven resemblance and its resolution are not addressed. Factual support is sparse with a material fold-name error.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. Balanced: divergence within c.2.1 with correct family examples, convergence across folds framed as most parsimonious but with the caveat that ancient relationships may be too faint to show (ECOD noted), correct fold vs superfamily semantics, global-evidence requirement, and transfer limits. Factual: family and fold examples (c.3, ALDH, sirtuin, DHFR, AKR) are correct but from memory and unverified against a release, flagged by the answer; refers to c.2 once as a 'class' before correcting to fold.

From memory and well disclaimed: correct direction (2.04 separate superfamilies/folds to shared b.18.1 superfamily, different families, structure-discovered) with rich multi-evidence discussion and no must_avoid breach. But hedges the release (2.07/2.08), omits the 2.04 ColG superfamily b.23.2, and omits family numbers b.18.1.36/b.18.1.3; identifiers sparse though b.18.1 correct.

Correctly keeps family-level homology and gives sensible template/dataset cautions (keep flag, stratify, no drop-in templates). But it misreads hf as a multi-chain/partial/non-standard construct record rather than SCOPe's heterogeneous-fold flag (different fold despite similar sequence and secondary-structure count), and says to 'expect a conserved core architecture' for both, violating the must_avoid on assuming geometry from family membership. No release, sunids, boundaries, comments, or evidence; hf definition unverified by its own admission. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 judge, 2026-10-22.

Good biological reasoning: homology unchanged, fragment caveats on alignment coverage and scores, complete well-resolved domain as representative, fragment retained only with partial label, conservative diversity interpretation, function transfer rejected. But explicitly from pretrained knowledge with no API evidence: no release, no domain boundaries, no sunids, and no statement of the actual SCOPe fr annotation semantics (missing >1/3 of common structure). Lineage given is correct. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-22.

Correct recommendation; family is strongest homology claim, new superfamily is agnostic and does not assert independent origin, new fold requires differing strand order/connectivity/core; rejects fold-based function, active-site and template transfer; lists evidence curators integrate (conserved residues, ligand sites, intermediate sequences); placement revisable across releases. sccs example a.1.1.1 is a valid notation example. No fabricated release facts. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Biological inference is complete: superfamily-level probable common ancestry, shared two-lobe Mg-ATP phosphotransfer core, explicit refusal to transfer substrate class or ePK regulation, PIKK/pseudokinase caveats, and full evidence list (family-level alignment, biochemistry, complex structures, regulatory architecture). Factual support is weak: no evidence bundle, superfamily d.144.1 given 'as I recall', and the required family identifiers d.144.1.7/d.144.1.6/d.144.1.4 are never stated (explicitly deferred to the user to check). Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-22.
